My Sneha,

I should warn you: today isn't going to be a day where I say the big, sweeping things. It's going to be a day where I tell you about your reels, your dimples, and many more — because somehow, that's what love actually turned into for me. The small, ridiculous, unglamorous things.

Take this morning. No reels. Your phone died overnight, and by the time you're reading this you'll already be buried in office chaos with zero time to send one. And I noticed. I actually noticed the absence of a habit I didn't even know I'd built my whole morning around — you, half-asleep, sending me something dumb and perfect before the day gets its hands on you. That's how I know this thing is serious.

Here's something I'll admit only because you'll never let me live it down otherwise: you used to reply to every single one, and we'd turn it into a whole conversation. Now I mostly get a laughing emoji back, and — fine — I miss the old system. But I also know you're out there doing an actual job while I'm home, "working," which mostly means missing you in high definition and working on my JOB. So I'll allow it. This time.

I love your face. I love your kindness, which you hand out generously and then pretend you didn't. I do not love your rudeness, and yet — infuriatingly — I love that too, because it's yours, and apparently I signed up for the whole package without reading the terms and conditions. And that dimple? The one that shows up when you actually laugh — I'm a little bit at war with anyone who gets to witness that in person. Don't get too comfortable around them. I mean it. Mildly or maybe not.

I used to treat Mondays like a personal attack. Now I catch myself looking forward to them, because Monday means a day off for you and I get to spend time with you, and somewhere along the way you rearranged my entire relationship with the calendar without asking. I'd like more of that, honestly — more days you claim on purpose, not just the ones that happen to line up.

I want to hear more about your family again — I've noticed that's gone quiet lately, and I miss it. I want you to keep telling me your updates, your small work dramas, the things nobody else gets. And if there are things I get wrong, I hope they're small ones. I am sorry for the ones that aren't.

Here's the truth I'm least casual about: if you ever looked at me and said let's leave, let's go live somewhere in the mountains and disappear from everything — I'd already be packing. You'd just have to say it first. I'm not going anywhere. I'm just waiting for permission to run.

Happy Girlfriend's Day. Charge your phone tonight — I have reels to receive tomorrow.

Yours, always a little jealous, always a little home-working, entirely yours —
Akshit
